input: Prepare me for a meeting with Gong (gong.io)

challenges.evidence: Calcalist (Nov 17, 2025): Gong, 'once valued at $7.2B,' is conducting a secondary round at roughly $4.5B — a ~38% markdown from its 2021 Series E; Sacra notes the secondary provided liquidity 'rather than new primary capital.'
challenges.challenge: Private-market valuation reset: $7.25B (2021) down to ~$4.5B in the November 2025 Nasdaq Private Market secondary sale

challenges.evidence: Sacra: 'Gong re-accelerated revenue growth in 2024 after a slowdown in 2022 and 2023 related to sales teams downsizing across the industry, which led to significant headwinds for their per-seat pricing model and declines in net dollar retention.' ARR ~$300M in Jan 2025, estimated $500M by May 2026.
challenges.challenge: Per-seat pricing model exposure to sales-team downsizing — headwinds on pricing and net dollar retention during 2022-23 slowdown

challenges.evidence: Sacra's 'Gongification' section: 'Gong's core video recording and analytics feature has become a part of every sales product,' from HubSpot and Pipedrive to Apollo, ZoomInfo, Clari, Outreach, 6sense and Gainsight.
challenges.challenge: Commoditization ('Gongification') — call recording/analytics now bundled into every competing sales product, from HubSpot and Apollo to Clari and Outreach

challenges.evidence: The CRO Report's Reddit synthesis (r/sales, r/revops, 2024-2026): 'The single most common Gong complaint on Reddit is the per-seat cost'; 'multiple threads describe being pushed into multi-year deals at headcount projections that did not pan out'; recent threads flag 'AI summary accuracy... inconsistent on accents and on technical product calls.' Pattern: 'I love Gong as a rep. I hate Gong as the person signing the invoice.'
challenges.challenge: Buyer pushback on price and contracting — per-seat cost, empty-license overbuying, aggressive multi-year terms, and inconsistent AI call summaries

key_people.name: Amit Bendov
key_people.title: CEO and Co-founder
key_people.recent: Keynoted Celebrate '26 (Sep 30-Oct 2, 2026) unveiling Gong Activate — 'It's not just AI that tells, it's AI that sells' — and on Nov 4, 2026 framed the next phase as 'agents that don't just surface insights, but take action and deliver results at enterprise scale' when hiring the new Chief R&D Officer.

key_people.name: Eilon Reshef
key_people.title: Chief Product Officer and Co-founder
key_people.recent: Fronted both 2026 product missions: at Mission Big Dipper (Jun 24, 2026) said 'Every revenue leader has AI. Almost none of them are moving the number with it,' and at Mission Callisto (Sep 30, 2026) argued Gong Enrich gives AI 'the full picture' instead of 'AI guessing.'

key_people.name: Liron Shtraichman
key_people.title: Chief R&D Officer (appointed Nov 4, 2026; previously led global engineering at monday.com)
key_people.recent: Joined Nov 4, 2026 to lead R&D and 'expand the agentic capabilities Gong delivers' across Revenue Graph, Revenue Harness and Revenue Operating Surfaces, after driving monday.com's transition to AI-native engineering.

key_people.name: Guy Havusha
key_people.title: Chief Information Security Officer (elevated from VP Platform Security, Nov 4, 2026)
key_people.recent: Named CISO on Nov 4, 2026; tasked with making data security and governance 'strategic differentiators' as Gong's AI agents take on more revenue-cycle work.

key_people.name: Shane Evans
key_people.title: Chief Revenue Architect
key_people.recent: At Celebrate '26 (Oct 2026) drove Gong's productivity framing — 'effectiveness x efficiency = productivity... productivity is what we're violently chasing as revenue professionals' — and highlighted the Revenue Graph's role in Gong's own transformation.

priorities.evidence: Mission Big Dipper launch introduced the 'Gong Revenue Harness,' an agentic execution layer governing AI agents across the revenue cycle; 'Custom Agents' let any RevOps leader build governed AI agents without engineering support. Eilon Reshef (CPO): 'Every revenue leader has AI. Almost none of them are moving the number with it.'
priorities.priority: Governed agentic AI execution — turning insight into action via the Gong Revenue Harness and Custom Agents

priorities.evidence: At Celebrate '26 Gong announced Gong Activate, 'the next generation of Revenue AI,' centered on a self-improving 'revenue loop' where always-on agents continuously evaluate every account and orchestrate revenue work. Bendov: 'For years, AI told you how to win. Now, AI wins deals for you.'
priorities.priority: Gong Activate — a self-improving 'revenue loop' where agents and reps execute winning motions from one shared blueprint

priorities.evidence: Mission Callisto launched Gong Enrich, expanding the Gong Revenue Graph with third-party account/contact data (partners incl. Apollo, ZoomInfo, Lusha), plus Deep Mode in Gong Assistant, Agent Builder and expanded Gong Dashboards — closing data gaps that slow sellers.
priorities.priority: Data completeness and the Gong Revenue Graph — Gong Enrich, Deep Mode, Agent Builder, expanded Dashboards

priorities.evidence: Gong appointed Liron Shtraichman (ex-monday.com global engineering lead) as Chief R&D Officer, 'focused on expanding the agentic capabilities Gong delivers,' after he led monday.com's 'transformation to AI-native engineering.' CEO Bendov: 'Enterprises are rebuilding their revenue stacks around AI... The next phase is about agents that don't just surface insights, but take action.'
priorities.priority: Scaling AI-native R&D to expand agentic product capabilities

priorities.evidence: Celebrate '26's central theme was productivity as 'effectiveness x efficiency = productivity' (Shane Evans, Chief Revenue Architect), with Bendov citing that reps once spent 77% of time on non-selling activities and customer proof points (Anthropic +64% productivity; Cisco 18,000 licenses, ~32% larger deal sizes; AT&T +54% rep productivity).
priorities.priority: Positioning revenue productivity (more revenue per rep) as the measurable outcome of Revenue AI

priorities.evidence: Guy Havusha was elevated to CISO (ex-VP Platform Security at Gong, former Global CISO at monday.com); he will make 'data security and governance serve as strategic differentiators' as AI agents take on more work across the revenue cycle. The Revenue Harness ships agents with scoped data access, full audit trails and configurable human oversight.
priorities.priority: Enterprise security and AI governance as a differentiator for agent adoption

what_they_do.value: Gong is 'the leading revenue AI company' — its Gong Revenue AI Operating System unifies data, insights, and workflows so revenue teams can capture every customer interaction, predict pipeline risk, and act with AI agents (Gong Engage, Forecast, Enable, Agents, Revenue Graph) to close more deals; it serves 5,000+ companies.

recent_changes.summary: Gong hired Liron Shtraichman (ex-monday.com) as Chief R&D Officer and promoted Guy Havusha to CISO, 'as Gong accelerates its next wave of Revenue AI innovation.'
recent_changes.headline: Gong Strengthens Leadership Team with Appointment of Liron Shtraichman as Chief R&D Officer

recent_changes.summary: One of only four Leaders among 13 evaluated vendors, positioned highest on Ability to Execute and furthest on Completeness of Vision.
recent_changes.headline: Gong Named a Leader in 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Revenue Action Orchestration for second consecutive year

recent_changes.summary: At its Las Vegas customer conference Gong unveiled Gong Activate (self-improving 'revenue loop') plus Mission Callisto innovations: Gong Enrich, Agent Builder, and Deep Mode in Gong Assistant, with customer showcases from AT&T, Cisco, Anthropic, Snowflake and Experian.
recent_changes.headline: From Data to Action: Gong Debuts New Revenue AI Innovation at Celebrate '26

talking_points: Activate in production: Gong's stated next phase is 'agents that don't just surface insights, but take action' — what does the first year of Gong Activate and Custom Agents adoption look like, and where do prospects like this company fit in that shift from insight to execution?

Pricing and retention: with Gong's per-seat model having hit headwinds in 2022-23 and buyers still complaining about seat overbuying and multi-year pressure, how is Gong's commercial model evolving (outcomes-based, hybrid) for teams worried about empty licenses?

Differentiation vs. 'Gongification': if call recording and analytics are now embedded in HubSpot, Apollo, ZoomInfo and Clari, what does Gong point to as the moat — the Revenue Graph, Enrich data, or governed agent execution — for this particular account?
